items.title: From Self to Others: A Motivational Theory of Intrapersonal and Interpersonal Growth
items.abstract: From Self to Others: A Motivational Theory of Intrapersonal and Interpersonal Growth delves into the intricate relationship between personal motivation and social development. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a compelling theory that connects the drive within an individual to understand and improve themselves (intrapersonal growth) with the equally important journey of building meaningful connections and influence in their social world (interpersonal growth). The book highlights how motivation acts as the essential catalyst bridging self-awareness with empathy, collaboration, and social engagement. This work articulates how nurturing motivation within the self creates pathways to authentic relationships, effective communication, and social harmony. By weaving together psychological insights and practical applications, Rachmad offers a framework that empowers readers to cultivate balanced growth for personal fulfillment and collective wellbeing. Published by UNICEF, this book underscores the universal relevance of harmonizing inner and outer development to foster resilient and compassionate communities. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad authored this book in 1996 as a response to the growing need for a unified understanding of how personal motivation influences social behaviors and vice versa. Recognizing the fragmentation in traditional motivational theories that focused narrowly on individual or social aspects, Rachmad sought to establish a comprehensive theory integrating both domains. The collaboration with UNICEF supported this vision, emphasizing global human development that values both personal insight and interpersonal relations. At its core, this theory distinguishes between intrapersonal growth—the deepening of self-understanding, emotional regulation, and self-motivation—and interpersonal growth—the development of empathy, communication skills, and social connectedness. Motivation is positioned as the dynamic force that activates and sustains growth in both spheres, creating a fluid movement from self-awareness toward meaningful social interaction. This theory emerged from observing how individuals with strong motivational foundations experience enhanced self-esteem and simultaneously engage more positively with others. Conversely, lack of motivation often impairs both self-improvement and social engagement. Societal complexities and rapid interpersonal demands further accentuate the necessity of this integrated motivational perspective. The motivational drive is both intrinsic and relational. Intrinsic motivation fuels personal insight and goal-setting, while relational motivation encourages social bonding and mutual support. These two aspects interact, enabling a cyclical growth pattern that reinforces both self and others’ development. Indicators include sustained self-reflection, purposeful goal pursuit, active listening, empathy in social exchanges, and constructive conflict resolution. Progress in these areas reflects the harmony between intrapersonal and interpersonal motivation. This framework operationalizes variables such as self-motivation intensity, emotional awareness, social engagement frequency, communication quality, and relational satisfaction. Measurement of these variables utilizes psychological scales, behavioral observations, and qualitative assessments. Factors that determine growth include individual personality traits, cultural values, environmental support, educational opportunities, and quality of social relationships. Rachmad stresses the importance of nurturing environments that cultivate both personal ambition and social responsibility. Effective implementation involves educational programs that blend self-awareness exercises with social skills training, community-building activities, mentorship, and reflective practices. UNICEF’s global outreach facilitates the adoption of these strategies in diverse cultural contexts. Challenges include cultural stigmas around expressing inner motivation, social isolation, and educational systems that neglect holistic motivational development. Supportive elements encompass inclusive policies, mental health advocacy, and programs promoting social cohesion. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that the fusion of intrapersonal and interpersonal motivation is essential for balanced human growth. This theory paves the way for individuals to achieve self-realization while fostering meaningful social contributions, ultimately enhancing collective human potential worldwide. items.title: Investigating the Impact of Subgraph Social Structure Preference on the Strategic Behavior of Networked Mixed-Motive Learning Agents
items.abstract: Limited work has examined the strategic behaviors of relational networked learning agents under social dilemmas, and has overlooked the intricate social dynamics of complex systems. We address the challenge with Socio-Relational Intrinsic Motivation (SRIM), which endows agents with diverse preferences over sub-graphical social structures in order to study the impact of agents' personal preferences over their sub-graphical relations on their strategic decision-making under sequential social dilemmas. Our results in the Harvest and Cleanup environments demonstrate that preferences over different subgraph structures (degree-, clique-, and critical connection-based) lead to distinct variations in agents' reward gathering and strategic behavior: individual aggressiveness in Harvest and individual contribution effort in Cleanup. Moreover, agents with different subgraphical structural positions consistently exhibit similar strategic behavioral shifts. Our proposed BCI metric captures structural variation within the population, and the relative ordering of BCI across social preferences is consistent in Harvest and Cleanup games for the same topology, suggesting the subgraphical structural impact is robust across environments. These results provide a new lens for examining agents' behavior in social dilemmas and insight for designing effective multi-agent ecosystems composed of heterogeneous social agents.

items.title: The Balance Within: A Motivational Theory of Emotional Intelligence and Resilience
items.abstract: The Balance Within offers an insightful journey into the intricate relationship between emotional intelligence and resilience, exploring how motivation rooted in emotional awareness cultivates inner strength. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a compelling theory that underscores the dynamic interplay between understanding one’s emotions and developing the capacity to bounce back from adversity. This book delves into the psychological and emotional mechanisms that empower individuals to maintain equilibrium amid life's challenges, promoting growth, well-being, and adaptive success. This work expands the boundaries of emotional intelligence research by integrating motivation as a critical driver for resilience, revealing practical approaches to nurture this balance within. Through thoughtful analysis and real-world examples, Rachmad provides a transformative framework that equips readers to harness emotional insights as a foundation for enduring personal and professional resilience. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad wrote this book in 1997, inspired by the growing recognition that resilience is not merely an innate trait but a skill deeply connected to emotional intelligence and motivation. Published by UNICEF, this work reflects a commitment to fostering resilient individuals capable of navigating increasingly complex social and emotional landscapes. At the heart of this theory lies emotional intelligence—defined as the ability to perceive, understand, and manage emotions—and resilience, described as the capacity to recover and thrive following setbacks. Motivation acts as the energizing force that bridges emotional insight with resilient behavior. Rachmad observed that individuals with high emotional awareness often demonstrate stronger resilience, but only when motivated by meaningful goals and internal drive. This linkage forms the basis for understanding how emotional intelligence and motivation coalesce to foster lasting psychological strength. The theory operates on the principle that cultivating emotional intelligence enhances motivation, which in turn reinforces resilience, creating a self-sustaining cycle of growth and adaptation. Key indicators include emotional regulation under stress, proactive problem-solving, optimistic outlooks, and the ability to learn from adversity. Variables central to this theory encompass emotional self-awareness, intrinsic motivation, coping strategies, and social support systems. Factors shaping the balance include individual personality traits, cultural background, environmental stressors, and available resources for emotional development. Rachmad advocates for programs that integrate emotional intelligence training with motivational coaching, emphasizing mindfulness, goal-setting, and reflective practices to build resilience. Supportive elements involve nurturing relationships and positive feedback environments, whereas challenges stem from stigma around emotional expression, lack of emotional education, and external pressures. In conclusion, The Balance Within affirms that emotional intelligence, powered by motivation, is foundational for resilience. This balance enables individuals not only to survive but to flourish through life’s difficulties, offering a hopeful blueprint for personal empowerment and sustained well-being. items.title: The Intellectual Intelligence Catalyst: How Deep Thinking Drives Personal and Professional Breakthroughs
items.abstract: This book explores the profound influence of deep intellectual engagement as the essential catalyst for remarkable personal and professional transformation. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a theory that positions thoughtful reflection, critical analysis, and intentional cognitive effort as the sparks igniting breakthrough achievements. Moving beyond superficial learning, this work highlights how sustained intellectual rigor fosters innovation, problem-solving mastery, and adaptive success in a complex world. Rachmad articulates how nurturing deep thinking not only amplifies intellectual capacity but also serves as a dynamic force empowering individuals to navigate challenges, seize opportunities, and realize their fullest potential. Through practical insights and illustrative cases, readers are guided to embrace the power of concentrated thought as a driver for meaningful change across all life domains. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad wrote this book in 1997 under the auspices of UNICEF, inspired by the emerging recognition that intellectual growth is most potent when rooted in deliberate, focused thinking. The author sought to bridge academic concepts with actionable strategies to help individuals leverage deep cognitive processes for breakthrough development. At the heart of the book lies the definition of deep thinking as reflective, critical, and sustained cognitive engagement that transcends routine knowledge acquisition. Intellectual intelligence, in this context, is the capacity to use such deep thinking to innovate, solve complex problems, and adapt effectively. The theory is grounded in observing how individuals who prioritize and cultivate deep intellectual focus consistently achieve significant advances in both personal and professional spheres. These breakthroughs often stem from moments of insight born from intense cognitive immersion. The catalyst effect occurs as deep thinking activates dormant intellectual resources, strengthens neural pathways, and generates novel perspectives leading to transformative outcomes. Indicators include sustained concentration, critical questioning, integrative reasoning, and the ability to connect disparate ideas meaningfully. Key variables include attention span, reflective capacity, cognitive endurance, motivation to explore complexity, and openness to new information. Essential determinants involve supportive environments that encourage inquiry, availability of time for contemplation, emotional readiness, and access to diverse knowledge sources. The book recommends creating structured time for reflection, fostering curiosity-driven inquiry, encouraging dialectical thinking, and building habits that sustain intellectual rigor. Supportive elements include mentorship, intellectual community, and encouraging feedback. Barriers involve distraction, time pressure, and cultural undervaluing of deep contemplation. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that deep thinking functions as a powerful catalyst unlocking intellectual intelligence’s transformative potential. By intentionally cultivating this capacity, individuals ignite a process of continuous breakthrough that reshapes their lives and work. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) is an Indonesian scholar, academic leader, and social development advocate with a strong multidisciplinary background. In 2016, YER was awarded the title of Doctor of Humanity, holds a Ph.D. in Information Technology and a DBA in Technology Management. Since 2016, YER has been actively teaching and collaborating with international universities in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the United States. YER is the founder of the Education Training Centre (ETC, 1992), YER Academic Publishing (YERA, 1993), the Multidisciplinary Academic Institute of Learning (MAIL, 1998), and YER E-Book Publishing (YERE, 1999), institutions dedicated to education, interdisciplinary learning, and ethical academic publishing. His academic contributions have led to his recognition as a Professor and his affiliation with the World Philosophy Foundation. YER is also actively involved in global development initiatives through the United Nations, as a member of the UN Global Compact (id-137635), the UN Global Market (id-709131), and the UN ECOSOC (id-677556). YER has served as a reviewer for several international journals and book chapters, and has written numerous books and articles on a wide range of topics including Philosophy, Economics, Management, With rich examples and practical insights, the book equips readers, educators, and leaders with tools to inspire and sustain intellectual advancement as a lifelong journey toward maximizing potential. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad developed this motivational theory in 1998 at UNICEF to address the growing need for a framework that connects the stimulation of intellectual intelligence with personal and societal growth. The work was inspired by observing how motivation fuels not just academic achievement but lifelong cognitive expansion. The book defines intellectual intelligence as the capacity to acquire, analyze, and utilize knowledge creatively and effectively. Motivation is framed as the energizing force that initiates and sustains this intellectual growth, making the two inseparable components of human development. The author noticed a widespread phenomenon: many individuals possess untapped intellectual abilities due to lack of motivation or inadequate motivational support systems. This inspired the need for a theory that bridges intellectual intelligence with motivational psychology. Intellectual growth thrives in environments where motivation—both internal curiosity and external encouragement—is nurtured. Learning becomes an active, self-directed process fueled by purpose and meaning. Observable markers include persistent curiosity, resilience in facing intellectual challenges, ability to integrate new knowledge, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. These involve motivational drivers (intrinsic interest, goal orientation), cognitive engagement (attention, memory), and environmental factors such as support networks and resources. The interaction between personal motivation, access to intellectual stimuli, social encouragement, and emotional well-being determine the extent of growth in intellectual intelligence. Rachmad suggests strategies including goal-setting, fostering curiosity through inquiry-based learning, creating supportive communities, and reinforcing success experiences to sustain motivation and intellectual expansion. Supportive elements include mentorship, positive feedback, and meaningful challenges; barriers encompass fear of failure, lack of encouragement, and cognitive disengagement. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that unlocking human potential hinges on understanding and leveraging the motivational forces that drive intellectual intelligence. This theory offers a robust framework to inspire growth, guide educational practices, and empower individuals to realize their fullest capacities. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) is an Indonesian scholar, academic leader, and social development advocate with a strong multidisciplinary background. In 2016, YER was awarded the title of Doctor of Humanity, holds a Ph.D. in Information Technology and a DBA in Technology Management. Since 2016, YER has been actively teaching and collaborating with international universities in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the United States. items.title: AI Disclosure with DAISY
items.abstract: The use of AI tools in research is becoming routine, alongside growing consensus that such use should be transparently disclosed. However, AI disclosure statements remain rare and inconsistent, with policies offering limited guidance and authors facing social, cognitive, and emotional barriers when reporting AI use. To explore how structured disclosure shapes what authors report and how they experience disclosure, we present DAISY (Disclosure of AI-uSe in Your Research), a form-based tool for generating AI disclosure statements. DAISY was developed from literature-derived requirements and co-design (N =11), and deployed in a user study with authors (N=31). DAISY-supported disclosures met more completeness criteria, offering clearer breakdowns of AI use across research and writing than unsupported disclosures. Surprisingly, despite concerns about how transparently disclosed AI use might be perceived, the use of DAISY did not reduce author comfort with the disclosure statements. We discuss design implications and a research agenda for AI disclosure as a sociotechnical practice.
